# Amadeus Life
简体中文 · Detailed configuration · Issues
Workspace-level autonomous activity, intentions and wake budgets.
Target package: **`@fg-lab/amadeus-life@1.2.1`**. Tested runtime baseline: official DSH Desktop **0.
2.1-rc.3**. MIT licensed.
## Release status
**1.2.1 is published:** GitHub Release · npm. Install the pinned version and verify the release chec
ksum. Later main changes do not change this immutable archive. See publishing policy.
## What you can do

- Track intentions and completed activity across a bound Workspace.
- Define controlled wake rules w
ith budgets, rate limits and execution boundaries; inspect activity history before enabling delivery

.
- Recognize trusted ordinary and QQ Session identities, including supported legacy IDs, without ta

king over QQ's immediate conversation loop.
- Configure rules and inspect state in the plugin's dedi
cated native DSH settings panels.
Example: record a follow-up intention and set a bounded wake rule for an authorized Workspace. Revie
w delivery state and budget use in the activity view.
Life is a scheduler, not a separate language model. External actions still require the appropriate t
ools and authorization. Optional QQ, Memory, State and Persona integrations do not grant additional
permissions. Keep wake delivery disabled until rules and targets are reviewed.
## Install and configure
Install the prebuilt `.tgz` with the official DSH plugin manager into your selected Profile. No loca
l source build is required. Follow installation instructions; do not copy configuration into a runni
equired. Follow installation instructions; do not copy configuration into a running Profile by hand.
Use native DSH settings to bind a Workspace, configure rules and budgets, then explicitly enable wak
DSH settings to bind a Workspace, configure rules and budgets, then explicitly enable wake delivery.
The other Amadeus plugins are optional. Install only the integrations you need.
## Interface
This is a recorded interface screenshot, not evidence that every real platform capability passed the
current release gate. See the detailed reference and verification reports for limitations.
## Upgrade and recovery
Back up user data before upgrading. Code, persistent user data and recovery backups are separate. Di
sable stops functionality; uninstall is intended to retain external data. Restoring old code alone d
oes not reverse a database migration.
